decisions.statement: A name format judges a name and writes a name.
The formats are the pages of this type rather than a list written in a check.
A format has the words of a name unchanged.
A format says only how the words are joined.
Converting between lower-kebab-case and lower-camel-case is owned by their pages alone.
A key in a format akasha defines is lower camel case.
A key in a format another system defines is spelled that system's way.

definition: how a name's parts are joined and capitalized

directives.name: Same Words Everywhere
directives.act: Give a name the same words in every place, in the format that place uses.
directives.warrant: The words have the meaning; the format belongs to the place.
aids: Change a name's format where it crosses over.
Never change its words to fit a format.
